Model277: Model277 is a four tap delay modelled on the Buchla 277. Patching an output back into an input builds a feedback loop, which overloads as the input level rises.
OUTPUT t — the delayed signal at the time set by the TIME knob.
OUTPUT t/2, t/3 and t/4 — three jacks carrying the delayed signal at a half, a third and a quarter of the time set by the TIME knob.
INPUT IN — four jacks, numbered 1 to 4, each feeding the delay line.
INPUT knobs 1 to 4 — one attenuverter per input, -1 to +1, setting the level of that input.
INPUT CV — four jacks, numbered 1 to 4, each setting the level of the input on that row.
TIME — the large knob, setting the delay time from 5ms to 200ms, default 100ms.
x 10 and x 1 — a switch; the x 10 position shifts the delay range to 50ms to 2000ms.
TIME CV — an input taking a signal that frequency modulates the delay time.
DEPTH — how far the TIME CV input moves the delay time, -0.5 to +0.5.
Logic: Logic is eight boolean gates: two AND, two NOT, two OR and two XOR. An input reads on at +1.00V or above, negative voltage is ignored, and every output sits at 0V or +5.00V.
AND — two gates, each with two inputs and one output; the output is on when both inputs are on.
NOT — two gates, each with one input and one output; the output is on when the input is off.
OR — two gates, each with two inputs and one output; the output is on when either input is on.
XOR — two gates, each with two inputs and one output; the output is on when one input is on and the other is off.
Socket colour — white sockets are inputs, black sockets are outputs.
Surveillance: Surveillance sends one source voltage to ten outputs, each output with its own attenuverter.
The large knob at the top sets the source voltage sent to all ten outputs.
RANGE — a switch; the 0v 10v position runs the source voltage from 0V to 10V, the -5v +5v position runs it from -5V to +5V.
GLOBAL CV IN — an input carrying a voltage to all ten outputs.
CTRL 01 to CTRL 10 — ten outputs, each with an attenuverter from -1 to +1 that scales and can invert the voltage sent to it.
PolyVoltageMeter: PVM reads a polyphonic cable and shows the voltage on each of its channels.
The input takes the polyphonic cable to be measured.
The rows down the panel show one reading per channel of the cable.
SQUONK: SQUONK is a twelve stage sequencer and programmer in the spirit of the Serge TKB. One stage is active at a time, and each stage holds five CV values, a trigger setting and a repeat count.
TRIG IN — one input per stage; a trigger there makes that stage the active one.
STAGE — one button per stage; clicking it makes that stage active, and the button of the active stage is lit.
x5 — one button per stage; lit green, it multiplies the five CV values of that stage by five.
A, B and C — three columns of knobs, one knob per stage, each setting a voltage from 0V to +2V that its column sends while the stage is active.
D and E — two columns of knobs, one knob per stage, each setting a voltage from -1V to +1V that its column sends while the stage is active.

MODE — one lamp per stage with four settings: yellow sends CV and a trigger, blue sends CV with no trigger, dark grey skips the stage when clocked, red sends the sequence back to the start step instead of playing that stage.
REP — one knob per stage, 1 to 8, splitting the clocked trigger of that stage into that many pulses.
TRIG OUT — one output per stage, firing when that stage is active.
GATE — one output per stage, high while that stage is the active one.
BRIDGE — one input and one output per stage; audio or CV at the input reaches the output while that stage is active.
OVER A — one input per stage; a voltage there replaces the A knob value of that stage.
OUTS A, B, C, D and E — the five CV outputs of the sequencer.
SEL — a knob that picks the active stage by hand, with a CV input below it that reads the voltage as 1V/oct.
CLK — a clock input that advances the sequencer one stage, with an output beside it passing the same clock on.
UP — a button and a trigger input; when on the sequence steps upward instead of downward.
RND — a button; when lit the next stage is picked at random.
ROT — a knob from -3 to +3 that rotates the MODE column by that many steps on each clock, with ROT-CV taking a voltage for the same.
LAST — an output firing each time a clocked sequence finishes a pass.
TRIG — an output firing whenever any stage trigger fires.
CHAIN A, B, C, D, E and CHAIN TRIG — inputs that take the five CV outputs and the TRIG output of a second SQUONK, so the two run as one longer sequence.
START, STOP and RESET — a button and a trigger input each, running, halting and resetting the sequencer; a reset lands on step 12, or on step 1 when UP is on.
RND ALL — a trigger input that randomises every setting, including x5, MODE and REP; the button beside it works only with the Cmd key held down.
Programmer: Programmer is a sixteen stage Serge style programmer. One stage is active at a time, and the four knob voltages of that stage appear at the four outputs.
1 to 16 — the numbers along the bottom, one per stage column.
A, B, C and D knob rows — one knob per stage in each row, setting the four voltages that stage holds.
A output — carries the voltage set by the A knob of the active stage.
B output — carries the voltage set by the B knob of the active stage.
C output — carries the voltage set by the C knob of the active stage.
D output — carries the voltage set by the D knob of the active stage.
ADDR — an input taking a voltage that picks which stage is active.
> — an input; a trigger there moves to the next stage.
< — an input; a trigger there moves to the previous stage.
The small knob at the top of each stage, marked 1 to 8, sets how many pulses that stage fires.
Nudger: Nudger is an expander for Programmer, with buttons and trigger inputs that step it forward and back.
« — five inputs down the left side, each with a button; a trigger or a click steps backward.
» — five inputs down the right side, each with a button; a trigger or a click steps forward.
CV ADD A, B, C and D — four inputs, each adding a voltage to the matching channel of Programmer.
Simpliciter: Simpliciter is a sampler. It plays a loaded or recorded sample at variable speed, holds a set of slices, and can record over itself while playing. It reads AIFF, 16bit and 24bit PCM WAV, and IEEE float WAV.
INPUT L in R — two audio inputs; with both patched the sound on sound section mixes them with the sample.
INPUT rec — a button and a trigger input starting a recording, and stopping it when used a second time.
INPUT mix — a knob setting the sound on sound blend; fully left is the internal signal, centre is half and half, fully right is the incoming signal.
INPUT sos — a switch turning sound on sound on and off.
PLAY HEAD varispeed — the large knob setting playback speed from -2 to +2, with 1.0 at the centre detent.
PLAY HEAD cv — an input that moves the playback speed, with a knob beside it setting how much of it is used.
PLAY HEAD oct — a knob shifting playback by octaves.
PLAY HEAD start — a button and a trigger input that start the sample playing.
PLAY HEAD pause — a button and a trigger input that stop playback and continue it.
PLAY HEAD gate — a switch; with it on the sample plays only while the gate is high.
PLAY HEAD loop — a switch that sets the sample to play round in a cycle.
OUTPUT L out R — the two audio outputs of the sampler.
OUTPUT eoc — an output sending a pulse each time playback reaches the end of the selection.
OUTPUT yummer — a switch and a level knob for an effect that spreads the grains of the sample in time.
zoom — a knob that magnifies the wave display without changing what plays.
slice grid — a knob setting how many equal slices the sample is divided into.
GRID on — a switch turning the grid over the sample on and off.
GRID peak — a switch that places the grid on the peaks of the sample rather than at equal spacing.
GRID sel — an input taking 0V to 10V to pick the current grid slice.
GRID rnd — a switch that picks the next grid slice at random at the end of each cycle.
SLICE MAKER save — a button and a trigger input storing the current selection as a new slice.
SLICE MAKER upd — a button and a trigger input writing the current selection over the slice now selected.
SLICE ASSEMBLER ◀ and ▶ — a button and a trigger input each, moving to the previous slice and to the next one and loading it.
SLICE ASSEMBLER sel — an input taking 0V to 10V to pick the current slice.
SLICE ASSEMBLER rnd — a trigger input that picks a slice at random from the stored set.
SLICE ASSEMBLER del — a button and a trigger input deleting the slice now selected.
ENGINE MOD wave — five shapes for the internal modulator: sine, triangle, sawtooth, square and sample and hold.
ENGINE MOD rate — a knob setting the frequency of the internal modulator, whose output is added to the playback speed.
ENGINE MOD depth — a knob setting how far the internal modulator moves the playback speed, with a CV input for the same.
ENGINE MOD clock — a pulse input; the speed of the pulses sets the frequency of the internal modulator in place of the rate knob.
ENGINE MOD sync — an input that resets the phase of the internal modulator.
ENGINE MOD uni and inv — two switches, one making the internal modulator unipolar, the other making it run negative.

Menu — the wave display carries the sample commands: reset the selection to the whole sample, trim to the selection, render the selection as the new sample, and cut, copy, paste, delete, invert, normalise and amplify.
Menu — a recording can be ended three ways: abandon it and free the memory, stop it and save it to a file, or stop it and append it to the current sample.
